blocks.html: When you send a WhatsApp message to a friend in Bhagalpur, your phone converts the words into signals, sends them through towers and cables, and your friend's phone turns them back into words. This exchange of data between two devices through a medium is called data communication.

rows: The device that sends the data
The device that receives the data
The data being sent: text, photo, audio, video
The path the message travels on
The set of rules both sides follow
FM radio, TV broadcast, keyboard to computer
Both ways, but one at a time
Walkie-talkie used by police; "over" ends your turn
Both ways at the same time

items.html: Twisted pair cable — pairs of copper wires twisted together to reduce interference. Cheap and common; used in landline phones and LAN cables (Cat 5e, Cat 6).
Coaxial cable — a central copper wire with insulation and a metal shield. Used for cable TV connections.

Optical fibre cable — carries data as pulses of light through thin glass strands. Extremely fast, long-distance and not affected by electrical noise. India's BharatNet project is laying optical fibre to connect gram panchayats.
Radio waves — travel long distances and through walls; used in FM radio, mobile phones, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.
Microwaves — need a clear line of sight between towers; used for long-distance links between mobile towers.
Infrared — very short range, cannot pass through walls; used in TV remote controls.
Satellite — a satellite in space receives signals and sends them back to another part of Earth. ISRO's GSAT satellites carry TV, internet and communication signals; DTH television uses satellites.

rows: No cable; signals travel through air or space
Easier to set up and allows movement
Difficult to lay over long or rough areas

blocks.html: Definition: A computer network is a group of two or more computers and devices connected together to share data, resources and services.

items.html: Resource sharing — one printer can serve the whole computer lab.
Data sharing — a school office can keep all student records in one place and use them from any desk.
Communication — email, chat and video calls.
Lower cost — one internet connection can be shared by many computers.
Backup — important files can be copied to a central server.
A virus can spread quickly to all connected computers.
Hackers may try to steal data, so security is needed.
If the main server or switch fails, many users are affected.

rows: Phone connected to earbuds and smartwatch by Bluetooth
Cable TV network of a city, city- wide Wi-Fi
The internet, bank networks connecting all branches

blocks.html: The topology of a network is the way its computers (nodes) are arranged and connected.

blocks.caption: Figure 3.1 · Network topologies: bus, star, ring and mesh

rows: Cheap, uses the least cable, easy to add nodes
If the main cable breaks, the whole network stops; slow with heavy traffic
Easy to install and manage; one faulty computer does not affect the others
If the central hub/switch fails, the whole network fails; needs more cable
Data flows in an orderly way; no collisions
A break in the ring can stop the network; adding nodes is difficult
Very reliable — if one link fails, data takes another path
Expensive; needs a lot of cable and ports

blocks.html: A tree topology joins several star networks to a main cable, like branches of a tree. A hybrid topology mixes two or more types. Most school and office networks today use a star topology built around a switch.

rows: Lets a computer connect to a network; each has a unique MAC address
Connects computers in a LAN; sends incoming data to all ports (simple and old)
Connects computers in a LAN; sends data only to the computer it is meant for (smarter than a hub)
Connects different networks and finds the best path for data; your home Wi-Fi router joins your home network to the internet
Modulator–demodulator; converts digital signals to signals that can travel on telephone or cable lines and back again
Boosts a weak signal so it can travel further
Lets wireless devices join a wired network (Wi-Fi)
Connects two networks that use different protocols

items.html: Client–server network: one powerful computer (the server) stores data and provides services; other computers (clients) request them. Example: when you check results on the board's website, your phone is the client and the board's computer is the server.
Peer-to-peer (P2P) network: all computers are equal and share directly with each other. Example: sharing files between two phones with a nearby-share app.

rows: High-speed internet, HD video streaming (4G spread rapidly in India from 2016)
Very high speed, very low delay; launched in India in October 2022

blocks.html: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be sent per second. It is measured in bits per second (bps): Kbps (thousand), Mbps (million), Gbps (billion).
Worked example: How long does it take to download a 100 MB video at 20 Mbps?
100 MB = 100 × 8 = 800 megabits. Time = 800 ÷ 20 = 40 seconds. (Note: b = bit, B = byte, and 1 byte = 8 bits.)
Did you know? Over 95% of the world's international internet traffic travels through optical fibre cables laid on the sea floor, not through satellites.
Aim: To find network details of a computer and test a connection.

items.html: Find your IP address. Open Command Prompt (type cmd in the Start search). Type

blocks.html: ipconfig and press Enter. Write down the IPv4 Address and Default Gateway.

items.html: Find the MAC address. Type ipconfig /all and note the Physical Address of your network adapter.
Test a connection. Type ping 8.8.8.8 and press Enter. Note the time (in ms) of each reply. Then ping your neighbour's IP address.
Check Wi-Fi. On a laptop, click the network icon on the taskbar. List the Wi-Fi networks you can see and note which are secured (lock symbol).
Share a folder. With your teacher's permission, right-click a folder → Properties → Sharing and share it with the lab network. Open it from another computer.
Draw your lab. Draw the network of your computer lab, showing computers, the switch, the router and the printer. Name its topology.

blocks.html: Record: Make a table of IP address, gateway and ping time for your computer.

items.html: Data communication needs a sender, receiver, message, medium and protocol.
Simplex is one-way, half-duplex is two-way one at a time, and full-duplex is two-way at the same time.
Wired media: twisted pair, coaxial and optical fibre. Wireless media: radio, microwave, infrared and satellite.
A network connects computers to share resources and data. By area: PAN, LAN, MAN, WAN.
Topologies are bus, star, ring, mesh, tree and hybrid; star is most common today.
Network devices include NIC, hub, switch, router, modem, repeater, access point and gateway.
Mobile networks grew from analog 1G to high-speed 5G.
